messages.subject: bug in io/writer.hpp:ordered_unconstrain
parts:
I was going through adding code for a positive_ordered type and I
think I've found a bug in io/writer.hpp:ordered_unconstrain.
Specifically, that function returns x[0] = log(y[0]) but the entries
of the ordered vector y don't need to be positive, hence y[0] could be
negative. I'm pretty certain this is a bug but it's possible I've
missed something.

Also, I'm almost finished implementing the positive_ordered type.
Ideally we would implement ordered<lower=??,upper=??> but that's more
complexity than I know how to deal with in the parser so in the
meantime I'm just implementing the positive case.

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] bug in io/writer.hpp:ordered_unconstrain
parts:
It used to be a positive ordered type!
The bug probably got introduced from my not fully
changing the behavior when the positivity
constraint was removed.

Yes, eventually having bounds would be a better
way to go. I can probably add that when I
add constraints to other types.

But not for v1.

- Bob
